question: Can a cross-validated, gradient-boosted regressor give lower and more uniform error than a standard MLP baseline when estimating a continuous physical quantity from robot-arm sensor readings on a public stand-in dataset?
method: OpenML kin8nm, one 80/20 split (fixed seed), inputs standardised on training data. Baseline: sklearn MLPRegressor. Improved: LightGBM with hyperparameters chosen by 5-fold CV on the training set plus sine/cosine features. Test-set MAE is the main metric; mean over three seeds.
baseline: scikit-learn MLPRegressor, two hidden layers of 64 units, early stopping, standardised inputs and target; stands in for the paper's CNN-RNN.
improved: LightGBM regressor with grid-searched hyperparameters (5-fold CV on the training set only) and sine/cosine features of the eight inputs.
notes: kin8nm is a simulated robot-arm dataset, not contact-force data; it is a stand-in only. The paper's neuromorphic-camera CRNN was not reproduced; the MLP is a generic baseline. Single train/test split; seeds vary model randomness only. Hyperparameters chosen by CV on training data; test set used once. Secondary metrics are RMSE, R^2 and the std of absolute error (uniformity proxy); classification F1 does not apply to regression.
